<a id="laws-of-the-hexagram-world-the-nuclear-law-the-cast-the-four-symmetries-the-counter-the-orbits--卦的世界上的律互之卦錯綜加一消息之六轨"></a>
# Laws of the hexagram world: the nuclear law, the cast, the four symmetries, the counter, the orbits

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`hexagram-world-laws` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](hexagram-world-laws.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> With no premise, along the runs of the spine: 互 merges and draws every run within two steps into 乾, 坤 and the turns of 既濟 and 未濟, the ends of the received order; turning lines settle in one step; 錯 and 綜 form a four-group of twenty classes; adding one has one orbit, waxing and waning six.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. The received order lists each configuration once, so a count over it is a count of configurations; a configuration a law leaves as it is stays along its run. (`Becoming.Hexagram.neither`, `Becoming.Hexagram.not_mem_of_memb`, `Becoming.Hexagram.distinctb`, `Becoming.Hexagram.nodup_of_distinctb`, `Becoming.Hexagram.order_nodup`, `Becoming.Hexagram.allUnbroken`, `Becoming.Hexagram.orbit_still`)
2. The nuclear law (互) takes lines 2 to 4 as the lower trigram and 3 to 5 as the upper. What it makes of a hexagram is fixed by the four inner lines, so two runs whose starts agree in them are one run from the first step; it merges (剝 and 坤 go on to 坤) and loses a possibility for good. (`Becoming.Hexagram.nuclear`, `Becoming.Hexagram.inner`, `Becoming.Hexagram.nuclear_inner`, `Becoming.Hexagram.run_inner`, `Becoming.Hexagram.nuclear_merges`, `Becoming.Hexagram.nuclear_process_merges`, `Becoming.Hexagram.nuclear_loses`)
3. Two steps of the nuclear law leave only lines 3 and 4, three times over, so two runs whose starts agree in them are one run from the second step. Lines 3 and 4, which swap at every step, are a lumping the law goes alike across; the count of unbroken lines is not (剝 and 比). (`Becoming.Hexagram.innerPair`, `Becoming.Hexagram.thrice`, `Becoming.Hexagram.nuclear_two`, `Becoming.Hexagram.nuclear_two_lumped`, `Becoming.Hexagram.run_two_middle`, `Becoming.Hexagram.thrice_inj`, `Becoming.Hexagram.innerPair_nuclear`, `Becoming.Hexagram.swap_eq`, `Becoming.Hexagram.innerPair_lumped`, `Becoming.Hexagram.innerPair_goAlike`, `Becoming.Hexagram.nuclear_yang_not_lumped`, `Becoming.Hexagram.nuclear_yang_not_goAlike`)
4. Along their runs 乾 and 坤 stay and 既濟 and 未濟 take turns, and a run stays where it starts exactly from 乾 and 坤. Every run is in these four from the second step on and every other configuration is drawn in, so exactly these four return: the first two and the last two of the received order. Four are in them, twelve enter at the first step and forty-eight at the second. 5. Lines 3 and 4 tell where a course comes to rest: at every even step from the second on the run is at them three times over; sixteen configurations go to 乾 (both unbroken), sixteen to 坤 (both broken) and thirty-two into the turns of 既濟 and 未濟 (where they differ). (`Becoming.Hexagram.thrice_back`, `Becoming.Hexagram.run_rests_at`, `Becoming.Hexagram.basin_iff`, `Becoming.Hexagram.and_of_both`, `Becoming.Hexagram.or_of_neither`, `Becoming.Hexagram.qian_basin`, `Becoming.Hexagram.kun_basin`, `Becoming.Hexagram.cycle_basin`, `Becoming.Hexagram.basin_counts`)
6. Keeping a hexagram, changing every line (錯), turning it over (綜) and both form a group of four in which each is its own inverse and any two commute. The nuclear law commutes with each, so each takes every run of it to a run of it; no configuration is its own complement, so the runs from a configuration and from its complement never meet, an instance of what a law commuting with a symmetry that moves everything keeps apart. (`Becoming.Hexagram.nuclear_complement`, `Becoming.Hexagram.nuclear_reverse`, `Becoming.Hexagram.complement_reverse`, `Becoming.Hexagram.reverse_reverse`, `Becoming.Hexagram.reverse_complement_reverse`, `Becoming.Hexagram.Symmetry`, `Becoming.Hexagram.Symmetry.act`, `Becoming.Hexagram.Symmetry.comp`, `Becoming.Hexagram.Symmetry.act_comp`, `Becoming.Hexagram.Symmetry.comp_self`, `Becoming.Hexagram.Symmetry.comp_comm`, `Becoming.Hexagram.Symmetry.act_self`, `Becoming.Hexagram.nuclear_act`, `Becoming.Hexagram.nuclear_run_act`, `Becoming.Hexagram.run_complement_apart`)
7. Named by its member of least binary value, a class holds the hexagrams a symmetry takes one to another: twenty classes, eight of two and twelve of four. The classes are a lumping the nuclear law goes alike across; the law of waxing and waning does not go alike across them, since turning over runs it backward. 8. The configurations turning over leaves as they are are exactly those the received order pairs by changing every line (乾坤, 頤大過, 坎離, 中孚小過); those turning over and changing every line take to one hexagram are exactly the pairs of the order in which the two agree (泰否, 隨蠱, 漸歸妹, 既濟未濟). 9. A marked line is turning (老) or staying (少); at the next step a turning line changes into its opposite and stays, and a staying one is as it was. Six marked lines show a hexagram (本卦) and, settled, go to one (之卦); settling twice is settling once, and lines are left as they are exactly where none turns. 10. The cast is a merging law settled in one step: along every run the lines are settled from the first step on and the run rests; one with a turning line is drawn into those with none, so a configuration returns exactly where no line turns. 11. The hexagram shown is not a lumping the cast goes alike across (乾 with every line staying and 乾 with its bottom line turning go on to 乾 and 姤); the hexagram the lines go to is. 12. Adding one, line 1 the lowest place, turns the lowest broken line and every unbroken line below it; taking one away undoes it, so it merges nothing. It has one orbit of sixty-four: every configuration can be had from every other, and each first comes back at the sixty-fourth step. <a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- No axiom and no premise: the laws, the marked lines, the symmetries, the classes and the orbits are defined in the module; each spine law is used at its stated hypotheses (Law.Drawn.not_returns with an absorbing region; Learning.goAlike_iff_lumped at the inner pair, the classes, the orbit and the hexagram gone to; Branching.law_returns_iff, law_merges_iff, law_keeps_iff and law_reach_iff on Law.process); the laws along runs hold for every run of the named law.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- What any passage says beyond these laws; the passage map of the chapter states, passage by passage, agreement, exact scope or divergence, and its readings are the AI's.
- The odds of old and young lines in the yarrow-stalk procedure (大衍); why the received order begins and ends where it does (it is not built from the nuclear law here); the nuclear trigrams of the 左傳 and 京房, not preserved here; whether 邵雍's 先天 sequence is the counter read with line 1 the highest digit (said in the module's documentation, not a theorem).
- That coming to rest, returning, turning or a class is good, fortunate or supports 生生; the module has no ethical predicate and no judgment of fortune.

**Standard boundaries:** No ethical premise and no Lean axiom is used. · Contains no ethical predicate and evaluates neither arising nor ceasing. · Stated for discrete steps. · A law of the formal model; its correspondence to actual systems is a separate obligation. · Names follow the structural naming criteria and are adopted only where the statement has their exact meaning; readings are interpretations, open to revision. · A relation omitted by a weaker description does not refute the fuller account.

The chapter on the 易传 maps 9 passages that cite this module: 4 agreements, 5 exact scopes and 0 divergences. Reading (the AI's, D51): 中爻 are lines 2 to 5, and what 互 makes is fixed by them (《繫辭下》 「非其中爻不備」), its judgment of right and wrong not in the law; the four where 互 rests open and close the received order; 錯 and 綜 name the complement and turning over, later names for what the text's 錯綜 does to numbers; 用九 and 用六 are the casts with every line turning, and 變則通，通則久 holds within the cast; adding one reads the divisions of 太極 as digits.
